frontier.hypothesis: The target's blocks 2/3 need a REUSED full-address value (one lui+addiu, then both lbu and sb at 0(reg)); every anonymous spelling measured emits two separate %hi materialisations instead, at the same instruction count. The untested question is whether an ordinary-C expression that is not a declared pointer object can produce a full-address value REUSED by both the read and the store inside one block.
frontier.mechanism: cse folds a constant symbol address back into the MEM's %lo when it can (giving lui+lbu %lo) and only forces a full-address pseudo when the address is not CONSTANT_ADDRESS_P at expand (s33's pseudo 75). g1's disassembly shows the fold happening independently at the read and at the store, so the value is never reused.
frontier.next_probe: Spell blocks 2/3 with an address expression that is non-constant at expand AND appears once as an lvalue base for both read and store within a single statement -- a compound read-modify-write on the anonymous expression (E |= K;) rather than the read/branch/store triple. Measure whether the RMW form emits lui+addiu+lbu+sb with a reused base, and at what score.

frontier.hypothesis: Live-range surgery on `q` is a three-seat problem, not two: g1 put q in $a1 and pushed p to $a0. If p's seat can be pinned to $a1 by ordinary C, the address object's remaining choice may narrow to $v1/$a0 and re-open quadrants s35 measured only in their p-displaced form.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocates by allocno priority; p and the address object are the only two long-lived pseudos, and tools/gcc-2.7.2/config/mips/mips.h defines no REG_ALLOC_ORDER, so their relative priority decides which takes $a0 and which $a1.
frontier.next_probe: Re-measure the g1/g5/g6 quadrants with p given an extra early use (or the s31 type-narrowing spelling) so its allocno priority rises above the address object's, and check whether p holds $a1 while the address object falls into $v1.
